last_analysis: Scores are hidden, so the trials can't be ranked. All nine trained without errors, and the two-seed noise is unknown. The search covered three families of ideas: recipes with more frequent updates (fewer envs, 1–3 epochs, gamma 0.97, lambda 0.95), placement heads that model the brick (learned footprint convolution, per-layer logsumexp head), and global attention. This is the last round, so each proposal combines parts that already train cleanly into a plausible best candidate. One gives the footprint-conv head the 1-epoch, ~400k-sample recipe (r3c2's recipe). One adds a cheap dilated residual conv to the footprint-conv model, which widens the receptive field without the cost of attention. One gives the per-layer head the 1-epoch recipe. All stay near 1–1.4x compute so they finish well inside the time limit. No result will tell me which recipe was better, because the scores are hidden, but the final selection uses the real dev scores.
